💲🎚The Proxy War Graduates

Marco Rubio already called Ukraine a “proxy war between nuclear powers.” 

Today Vladimir Putin supplied the next chapter: he told the Valdai Discussion Club that international conflicts are highly likely to continue, blamed the upheaval on the decline of Western hegemony, and warned the West against escalation. 

He also said Russia would use “all weapons at [its] disposal” if attacked. 

This is the logic of a proxy war after it has run too long. Washington says it is helping Ukraine defend itself. Moscow says it is fighting the West through Ukraine. 

Both states preserve the line that keeps their own soldiers from meeting openly, while Ukraine remains the place where the line is paid for in bodies and ruins.

Putin’s threat is not a peace proposal. It is a demand that NATO stay outside the ring while Russia continues fighting inside it. The Kremlin’s promise to reach for its entire arsenal if Russia is attacked gives the arrangement its nuclear perimeter. 

Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico recently described the same machine more crudely, calling the Western effort to defeat Russia through Ukraine a failed strategy and warning that some Western politicians want a direct NATO-Russia confrontation. 

Rubio called it a proxy war. Putin calls it Western hegemony. 

Fico calls it an attempt to destroy Russia. Everyone has a phrase. Ukraine has the cemetery.
